jobs.description:
The Analytical Center of Excellence (ACE) organization is looking for a 
Junior Analytical Technician 
(full shift) in the Chemicals lab located in Terneuzen, The Netherlands.
 

The Chemicals lab in is one of the Manufacturing Production Quality (MPQ) labs that performs analysis of plant-samples in Terneuzen. Servings multiple production plants such as polyurethanes and polyglycols results in the need for a 24/7 service and a full-shift roster to perform the analysis of all plant samples.
 

Responsibilities
 
 

• Ensure service requests are accurately run, and the data returned as per sample plan. 

• Analytical equipment operations and troubleshooting as per procedures. 

• Provide input of quality data into LIMS, document and communicate results. 

• Perform calibration and first line-maintenance of analytical equipment. Document/administrate these maintenance activities. Communicate maintenance work when required. 

• Apply Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S), Analytical Work Process and Operating Discipline/Quality System procedures and practices as well as cGMP/pharma standards. 

• Participating in and completing of laboratory training and corporate required trainings. 

• Co-operate and communicate with co-workers and clients to maintain workflow and instrumental information, and to share and leverage problem solving and prevention expertise. 

• Contribute to value creation by continuous improvement of procedures in the analytical work processes and related tools and performance metrics. 

• Promote a well-organized, responsive, efficient workplace and work well both as a team member and independently. 

Qualifications
 
 

• MBO-4 laboratory degree or similar (bachelors degree preferred). 

• Fluent in Dutch and English. 

• Experience in an industrial laboratory (analytical) 

• Able to work in full shift (24/7 roster): morning, afternoon and night shifts.  

 
 

Preferred qualifications
 
 

• GMP/pharma experience. 

• Experience in operation, calibration, maintenance and troubleshooting of analytical equipment. 

• Knowledge of quality data systems like LIMS, OpenLab, etc. 

• Good lab techniques, methodical record keeping, and the ability to work both independently and with co-workers. 

• Excellent human relations, organizational and communication skills are necessary to communicate with team members, partners and outside customers. 

• Exhibit confidence in confirming validity of methods and data. 

• Able to handle multiple tasks and work under pressure.

Main Responsibilities of the role:
Preparation and formulation of vaccines and pharmaceutical products.
Working with fixed and mobile brewing kettles up to 5000 liters.
Preparation, control and release of raw materials, filters and materials.
Execution of CIP and SIP processes on plants and equipment.
Registration of process steps and checks according to GMP and GDP guidelines.
Identifying and resolving deviations and process disruptions.
Collaborating with colleagues from production, quality, planning and technical operations.
Contributing to improvement projects and optimizations within the department.

Required Qualifications and skills
You love technology, processes and quality. You work accurately, take responsibility and enjoy achieving results together.
A completed MBO-3, MBO-4 or HBO education (e.g. MLO, MTS, VAPRO or similar).
Interest in engineering, process technology or pharmaceutical production.
A proactive and inquisitive attitude.
Good communication skills.
An eye for quality, safety and detail.
Experience within GMP, pharmaceuticals, food or process industry is a plus, but not a requirement.
Fluent in Dutch and English.

 Hi! Candlelight, live music and a room that goes completely quiet the moment the first note lands. That is your Friday or Saturday evening. We are hiring event crew for live music events at some of the most beautiful venues in the country. Old churches, hundreds of candles, a few hundred guests who came for one unforgettable concert. You work around 16 to 21 hours a week, always in the weekend. 
 Four cities, and you pick yours 
We run these events from four home bases: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Groningen and Nijmegen. You choose the city closest to you and that becomes your base. You are not sent all over the country. You work in the region you already live in, with the same team every time. 
 How the hub works 
Every city has one meeting point, usually the central station. We call it the hub. Before a shift you meet your team there, and from the hub you head to the venue together by car. 
Sometimes the venue is right in the city. Sometimes it is a beautiful church half an hour outside it. Either way, everything from the hub onwards is arranged and paid for by us. All you have to do is get yourself to the hub. 
 Your evening 
Arrive at the hub and travel to the venue. Build the room and set the candles. Open the doors and welcome the guests to their seats. Help the artists find their way. Keep everything running during the show. Clean up with the team when the last guest has left. 
 What you get
